reason: E2 supports that heterogeneous lattice strain causes unusual dislocation behaviors, but does not link this to short-range order or toughness. E1 shows nano-twinning enhances toughness in CrCoNi, but does not connect it to short-range order or lattice strain heterogeneity. The core premise that short-range order governs toughness via strain heterogeneity is not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Short-range chemical ordering creates local lattice strain heterogeneity in single-phase HEAs.
This strain heterogeneity causes non-uniform dislocation motion and concentrated stress fields.
Reducing short-range order (e.g., by homogenization) promotes uniform dislocation motion and nano-twinning.
Uniform plasticity delays crack nucleation, enhancing toughness retention.
Nano-twinning is a beneficial deformation mode that alleviates strength-toughness trade-offs.
